bottleneck: Lentiviral and retroviral vectors integrate semi-randomly into the genome, and integration near oncogenes can activate them — the SCID-X1 trials caused leukemia in several children via LMO2 activation. Modern self-inactivating vectors reduce but do not eliminate the risk, and integration-site analysis can only characterize, not prevent, dangerous insertions. Every integrating therapy therefore carries a latent oncogenic lottery ticket, with the draw occurring years after treatment when surveillance may have lapsed.
current_state: SIN lentiviral vectors are in approved products (e.g., CAR-T, Libmeldy) with monitoring for clonal expansion. No integrating vector is proven risk-free, and long-term registries are still maturing.

sources.title: Architecting the Future of Health: From Code to Cure

title: Insertional mutagenesis risk in integrating vectors
why_it_blocks: A cure that can cause leukemia is a cure regulators will gate heavily. Insertional risk keeps integrating vectors under lifelong surveillance and blocks their use where safer alternatives do not exist, narrowing the treatable population.
